product: BricsCAD (Bricsys / Octave, a Hexagon company) - V25/V26, Pro/BIM/Ultimate
summary: User sentiment 2024-2026 is positive on the volume sites (G2 4.5/5 on 135 reviews; SaaSWorthy 4.7/5 on 131) and the pitch that works is 'AutoCAD-compatible, much cheaper, perpetual licence still sold'. The loudest negatives are stability regressions in each yearly release (V25.1-25.2 panning/autosave crashes with an MTFLAGS=0 workaround, users rolling back to meet deadlines; V26.1.08 more crashes on macOS), a macOS build users call a 'perpetual beta' (freezing, no clear native Apple-silicon binary, Metal renderer slower than OpenGL), a second-class Linux build (Wayland black window), large-drawing/3D performance, dynamic blocks (creation only arrived in V26, experimental and unavailable to US users for licensing reasons), uneven support responsiveness (Capterra support 3.9 vs ease-of-use 4.6), and a January-2026 upgrade/support policy that forum users call a 'cynical move' against old perpetual licences. No direct user reviews of the native civil tools surfaced; the market treats a third-party add-on (Civil Site Design) as the Civil 3D alternative on BricsCAD, implying the native TIN/alignment/corridor stack is incomplete for site design. LIMITS: ten searches only (shared budget exhausted) and every target host was denied by the environment's network policy, so all items are paraphrased from search-engine summaries, not opened pages; no Reddit or Hacker News threads were captured; BIM usability and LISP-compatibility themes were not reached.

aggregate_ratings.rating: 4.5/5 (AI sub-scores: ease of setup 9.1, quality of support 9.0)
4.5/5 (ease of use 4.6, customer service 3.9); starting price shown $590 one-time

10/10 trScore on the reviews page (9.4–9.5/10 on other crawls); BricsCAD's own rendering/visualization feature score is 8.0 from one rating (the 6.6 first reported was the category average: corrected by the fact-check)

praise.detail: G2 reviewers say it is easy to learn for AutoCAD users because it operates similarly; opens DWG, makes clean PDFs, supports AutoCAD LISP routines and toolbars. A reseller's 'about a day of retraining' claim is marketing, not a user.

'Costs much less than AutoCAD, with one-time license options' is the most repeated praise; TrustRadius reviewer: a cheaper alternative to AutoCAD LT; AlternativeTo commenter: does everything they did in AutoCAD LT. Independent V26 review confirms perpetual licensing remains available alongside subscription.
Forum commenter: maintenance is about 60% cheaper than buying an upgrade each year; another reported a $236 upgrade-to-new-perpetual price confirmed by Bricsys sales (single-user claims).
G2 AI summaries score ease of setup 9.1 and quality of support 9.0; the MTFLAGS=0 crash workaround came from Bricsys support engaging on the forum.
TrustRadius reviewers note strong compatibility with AutoTURN vehicle-tracking; reseller KTF praises V26 'Auto Mapping for Civil Points'.

Independent Drafting Bench review calls V26 'a year of maturation' (released 26 Oct 2025; V26.2 on 31 Mar 2026 carried most new capability incl. AI 'BricsCAD Assist' panel and dynamic-block creation). Vendor claims 60+ features, up to 25x faster 3D solid edits and 2.7-2.8x faster DWG file ops - unverified company figures.
Linux users report it runs and feels slightly more stable than the Mac build; a 2022 viewport-lag thread traced the cause to NVIDIA driver setup rather than BricsCAD.

praise.theme: LISP runs, and runs faster (added from the editor's own web search on 2026-10-21)
praise.detail: Consultants who migrated large custom environments report nearly all AutoLISP files ran unchanged, with minor system-variable and command-line differences; one benchmark had a routine run three times faster than in AutoCAD (vendor-affiliated sources)

complaints.theme: Crashes and stability regressions in V25
complaints.detail: Jan 2025 V25.1.07 fatal errors while panning/zooming (support workaround MTFLAGS=0; AMD black-screen crashes after update); Apr 2025 V25.2.03 copy-then-pan crashes, a user reinstalled an older build to meet a deadline; Aug 2025 'V25 considerably worse than V24', one user's fifth crash in three hours on a simple model; Mar 2025 crashes on close/autosave and a suspected save bug. Forum anecdotes, not Bricsys-confirmed.

complaints.theme: Bugs make it unusable for some professional work
complaints.detail: Capterra March 2025 German review rated 1/5: unusable for professional architecture work due to performance problems and bugs. SaaSWorthy lists 'occasional instability' as a weakness.

Thread 'BricsCAD for Mac seems to be a perpetual beta app': freezing, beachballs, GUI glitches, missing Windows parity for years; a user says the Mac build is still Intel-only (Wikipedia says Apple-silicon compatible - unresolved, possibly Rosetta); 2025 move to Metal reported as much slower than the old OpenGL path; 'a lot more crashing since V26.1.08' and V26 unable to save some files V25 handles.

Wayland black window plus crash report with GDK assertion on 25.2.03; users say Linux and Mac share the same GUI flaws and unexpected crashes and do not match the Windows experience; desktop-integration quality thread.

complaints.theme: Performance on large drawings and in 3D
complaints.detail: G2 common con: large-file handling performance; forum: massive lag selecting objects with the Structure Browser open, 3D viewport lag across platforms, Windows memory usage; G2: parametric blocks weaker than AutoCAD's and can slow things down.

complaints.theme: Dynamic blocks incomplete; V26 creation withheld in US
complaints.detail: TrustRadius con: incomplete dynamic-block support. V26 adds Dynamic Block creation/editing but the independent reviewer says it is still experimental and unavailable to US users because of licensing (reason unverified).
G2: a few AutoCAD commands and tools are not available or less polished; minor differences show up during complicated operations.

complaints.theme: Licensing policy shift against old perpetual licences (1 Jan 2026)
complaints.detail: New Upgrade and Support Policy: support covers latest + three previous versions, but owners of very old perpetual licences can no longer upgrade without maintenance; thread calls it 'a cynical move'; users say maintenance keeps rising and the policy pushes toward subscription. Maintenance figures seen: EUR 710/yr Pro (Bricsys page) vs EUR 440/yr renewal on the Ultimate page (inconsistent, unverified) and $292 Pro at NOVEDGE. No evidence of a specific 2025 price rise.

Capterra customer-service sub-score 3.9 vs 4.6 ease of use; Trustpilot reviewer: registration-code requests unanswered; G2 compare pages list support response time as a common complaint - while G2's summary scores support 9.0.
A .NET plug-in that worked in V24 crashed at V25 start-up; 'Error loading lrx file V25' thread.

No user review of the native civil tools was captured. Structural evidence: the third-party Civil Site Design add-on is marketed on BricsCAD as 'the best Civil 3D alternative' and imports Civil 3D surfaces/alignments, implying the native TIN/alignment/corridor tools (spirals, parabolic vertical curves, CORRIDOR since V21) are not a complete site-design stack (pipe networks, labels, plan production). Inference, unverified.
G2: difficulty learning due to limited resources; comparison site: smaller user community than AutoCAD, fewer forums and third-party resources; SaaSWorthy: steep learning curve for some features.

TrustRadius con: dated-looking interface. The earlier note that rendering/visualization scored 6.6 was wrong: 6.6 is the TrustRadius category average, BricsCAD's own score is 8.0 from a single rating (fact-check, 2026-10-21)
G2 and vendor pages now carry the 'Octave' name (Hexagon spin-off branding; details unverified) and BricsCAD Shape was discontinued as a standalone product with V26 per Wikipedia (summary only).

complaints.theme: V26 regressions: LISP, MLINE, STEP import, slowdowns (added from the editor's own web search on 2026-10-21)
complaints.detail: Forum threads in late 2025 and 2026 report mature AutoLISP routines terminating early or freezing in V26, multi-MLINE Trim/Extend failing (a changed TRIMEXTENDMODE default is one explanation), a Communicator STEP import hang, 'performance slowdowns' and 'non stop crashing' in Mechanical V26; several posters reverted to V25, which also means a separate Communicator rollback

complaints.theme: Upgrade experience (added from the editor's own web search on 2026-10-21)
complaints.detail: A forum thread titled 'New release, the usual rubbish upgrade experience' collects complaints about each yearly version's installation and migration friction

wishes: A stable x.0 release each year - stop shipping regressions that force users to roll back (V25.1/25.2 crash threads).
A native Apple-silicon macOS build with Windows feature parity and a Metal renderer no slower than the old OpenGL path.
Full Wayland support and polished Linux desktop integration.
Dynamic-block creation available to all users including the US, and out of 'experimental'.
The remaining missing or less-polished AutoCAD commands closed.
Keep affordable perpetual upgrades for old licences; stop raising maintenance; no push to subscription.
Faster, more reliable support tickets and licence/registration handling.
More tutorials, documentation and a larger community.
A plug-in API (.NET/BRX/LRX) that does not break at each yearly version.
Less dated UI and better rendering.
(Inferred) native civil tools complete enough for site design without a third-party add-on.

key_claims.claim: G2 rates BricsCAD 4.5/5 on 135 reviews (page title 'Octave BricsCAD').
Capterra rates BricsCAD 4.5/5 on 18 reviews with customer service 3.9 and ease of use 4.6; a March 2025 review gave 1/5 for bugs and performance.

TrustRadius shows 10/10 on 11 ratings (2 written reviews); BricsCAD's rendering/visualization score is 8.0 from one rating, 6.6 being the category average (corrected by the fact-check); incomplete dynamic-block support is listed as a con
V25.1.07 users got fatal errors while panning/zooming; Bricsys support's workaround was MTFLAGS=0.
A V25.2.03 user rolled back to an older build to meet a deadline because of panning crashes.
An Aug 2025 forum user judged V25 considerably worse than V24 for crashes and performance.
Mac users describe BricsCAD for Mac as a 'perpetual beta' with years of freezing and parity gaps.
A forum user says the Mac build is Intel-only with no native Apple-silicon version (conflicts with Wikipedia's 'Apple Silicon compatible'; unresolved).
BricsCAD V26 was released 26 Oct 2025, V26.2 on 31 Mar 2026; dynamic-block creation is experimental and unavailable to US users; perpetual licensing remains available.
A new Upgrade and Support Policy effective 1 Jan 2026 covers latest + three previous versions and ends upgrades for very old perpetual licences without maintenance; forum users call it cynical.
Vendor claims V26 is up to 25x faster for 3D solid edits and 2.7-2.8x faster for DWG file operations than V25 (unverified).
Civil Site Design is marketed as the Civil 3D alternative on BricsCAD, reading Civil 3D surfaces and alignments directly.

No Reddit or Hacker News threads were captured (the Reddit-targeted and site:news.ycombinator.com searches returned none) and all review/forum hosts were blocked by the environment's network policy, so every item is paraphrased from search summaries, not opened pages.
